text:
Kennel doors, minutes at dawn
The agenda began with it

Attendees were Leo Dubois, Jonah Williams, Teddy, and the rest of the Companion Animal Travel Desk team.

The group opened with a calm review of the check-in flow for traveling pets and their handlers. <<FACT F092>> The talk stayed practical, with everyone agreeing that clear handoffs make the start of a journey feel less rushed for both people and animals. There was also a reminder to keep the welcome area tidy and quiet, since a soft first impression helps nervous pets settle in better.

The welfare coordinator shared a few notes on comfort checks, including water access, carrier fit, and simple signs of stress to watch for before boarding. The team liked the idea of using the same friendly words each time a family arrives, so the process feels steady and easy to follow. Teddy came up as a cheerful example in the discussion, with the room agreeing that familiar scents, gentle voices, and a patient pace do a lot of good for small travelers.

Next, the desk talked through coordination with the larger airport flow at Aurelia Skyways. The members noted that short updates between the desk and the welcome team help avoid confusion near boarding, especially when a passenger needs a little extra time. Someone also suggested keeping a written reminder list close by, so the most important comfort steps are never missed during a busy stretch.

The meeting closed with support for a warmer greeting routine and a request to keep sharing small observations from daily work. Everyone left with the sense that the Companion Animal Travel Desk is doing thoughtful work and that steady teamwork keeps each trip smoother than the last.

The meeting ended with good spirits and clear next steps.
